summary: Within the fixed window 2026-09-11T17:27:19Z–17:32:19Z (policy m004-fault-window, integration m0-otel-20260909), the user-visible failure is POST /api/checkout returning 500 via_upstream at the frontend-proxy edge, and it traces to the payment dependency: checkout spans for oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder carry otel.status_code=ERROR / rpc.grpc.status_code=13 with the description 'failed to charge card: could not charge the card: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = Payment request failed. Invalid token', while payment spans for grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge carry the same message with a stacktrace pointing at module.exports.charge (/usr/src/app/charge.js:37) in the payment container (service.version 2.0.2, host 8d8e65e2ed9f). The proxy's 500 log row, the checkout error span and the payment error span all share trace_id c5b88bf37781c7a44fa58df56c19fc9e. Error counters increased over the window (extrapolated increase over 5m: checkout 17.09, frontend 25.64, payment 8.55 error spans), but trace views are truncated/sampled (7 of 9 returned traces visible; 276–278 spans omitted) and no parent references are visible, so the checkout→payment call edge is a well-grounded inference, not a directly observed parent-child edge. The underlying reason payment rejects the token is not determinable from the authorized telemetry (no payment logs; no configuration data) and remains unknown. Cart is not implicated. No SLO or baseline was supplied, so no health/recovery certification is made.

Trace c5b88bf37781c7a44fa58df56c19fc9e appears in three independent views: the frontend-proxy 500 access log row (trace_id field), the checkout PlaceOrder error span, and the payment Charge error span; the same trace-id co-occurrence of the checkout and payment error spans also holds for traces 69e7fcd253f200859acff824ce558ed1, ab1a5608703b83a8ba5ea4751569651f, c0baa50f88c529912bb1a1a431fa3b09 and d5eb47bc2cf60eacef3fdbdca987a0d8.

Error counters are cumulative at instant evaluation time 1789147939: checkout status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR had raw value 16 while STATUS_CODE_UNSET had 260 (cumulative since reset, not a window count). Explicit window deltas: sum by service of increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m]) returned checkout 17.0947, frontend 25.6421, payment 8.5474 (extrapolated, fractional, not unique request counts); total span-call increase over 5m per service included frontend 640.76, frontend-proxy 306.92, cart 223.34, checkout 94.45, payment 19.78.

app_payment_transactions_total for service_name=payment evaluated to 14 at 1789147939; the expression's result carried no status_code/rpc_method/error label values, so no success/failure split can be derived from it, and as a raw counter value it does not establish in-window transaction events.

Cart is not the failing dependency in this window: cart has error_spans_by_listed_status_tags 0 in the returned trace artifacts, and all 20 displayed cart log rows (backend_total_hits 81) are severity Information for GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync, including rows in trace c5b88bf37781c7a44fa58df56c19fc9e at 17:32:11.656Z — the same trace as the checkout 500.

Most likely failure path: payment's PaymentService/Charge rejects the charge ('Payment request failed. Invalid token'), checkout's PlaceOrder consequently fails (grpc code Unknown/13, 'failed to charge card'), and the frontend/frontend-proxy surface it as HTTP 500 on POST /api/checkout. Grounded in matching trace ids and error text across proxy, checkout and payment views plus the in-window error-counter increases; the parent-child edge itself is not visible (parent_is_visible=false in every displayed span), so this edge is inferred, not directly observed.

Provisional: the rejection is generated inside payment itself by an explicit token-validation failure at charge.js:37 (error name 'Error', grpc code Unknown, message mentions app.loyalty.level=gold), i.e. a code-level rejection rather than an observed crash or transport failure. What makes the token invalid (client-side token generation, token/secret material, or a payment-side validity expectation) is not observable in the authorized telemetry and is not established here.

The trace evidence is a biased, truncated sample, not a complete call chain: of 9 returned traces only 7 (checkout query) and 5 (payment query) were visible, 276–278 spans were omitted, error-detail fields were omitted (97–103 per view), display_max_spans is 20, and no popped span had parent_is_visible=true — so no complete checkout→payment chain, population failure rate, or per-request uniqueness can be asserted. Logs cover only cart and frontend-proxy; payment/checkout log lines were not available.
